scenes.tts: Every excitatory neuron of the mouse cortex is born at the bottom, in the zones beside the ventricle. So how do the layers get in order?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Wall of the Brain. A tall slice of embryonic cortical wall, ventricle at the bottom, pia at the top, with a single excitatory neuron sitting in the zones at the bottom. Question on screen: how do the layers get in order?
scenes.narration: Every excitatory neuron of the mouse cortex is born at the bottom, in the zones beside the ventricle. So how do the layers get in order?

scenes.tts: Notch and Numb can make two sisters different at a division. But a yes or no alone cannot say which division it was.
scenes.visual: A dividing cell splits into two sisters, one tinted Notch-on, one tinted Numb. Label: sister versus sister, at one division.
scenes.narration: Notch and Numb can make two sisters different at a division. But a yes or no alone cannot say which division it was.

scenes.tts: A stem cell that makes ten different daughters needs more than that. What tells the tenth daughter she is not the first?
scenes.visual: A stem cell divides ten times in a row; ten daughters line up, each with a blank tag. Question: ten daughters, ten different types?
scenes.narration: A stem cell that makes ten different daughters needs more than that. What tells the tenth daughter she is not the first?

scenes.tts: Picture a slice through the wall of the embryonic mouse forebrain. The ventricle is at the bottom, the pia on top.
scenes.visual: Zoom from a mouse embryo head to a vertical strip of the forebrain wall. Labels appear: ventricle (bottom), pia (top).
scenes.narration: Picture a slice through the wall of the embryonic mouse forebrain. The ventricle is at the bottom, the pia on top.

scenes.tts: The ventricular zone lines the ventricle. Many of its progenitors are radial glia. They divide and send a long fibre up to the pia.
scenes.visual: Bottom band labelled ventricular zone fills with progenitor cells. Many are radial glia; one sends a thin fibre all the way to the pia.
scenes.narration: The ventricular zone lines the ventricle. Many of its progenitors are radial glia. They divide and send a long fibre up to the pia.

scenes.tts: Just above sits the subventricular zone. Intermediate progenitors, daughters of radial glia, divide there, usually to make neurons.
scenes.visual: A second band above, labelled subventricular zone. A radial glial daughter moves up into it and divides into two neurons.
scenes.narration: Just above sits the subventricular zone. Intermediate progenitors, daughters of radial glia, divide there, usually to make neurons.

scenes.tts: The first neurons form a thin sheet just under the pia. This is the preplate.
scenes.visual: A thin sheet of neurons, labelled preplate, appears directly under the pia. The middle of the wall stays empty.
scenes.narration: The first neurons form a thin sheet just under the pia. This is the preplate.

scenes.tts: The next neurons arrive in the middle of the preplate and wedge it apart.
scenes.visual: Three-frame inset: preplate intact; new neurons arriving in its middle; the sheet pushed apart into an upper and a lower half.
scenes.narration: The next neurons arrive in the middle of the preplate and wedge it apart.

scenes.tts: The top half becomes the marginal zone, future layer one, home of the Kahal Retzius cells. The bottom half becomes the subplate.
scenes.caption: The top half becomes the marginal zone, future layer 1, home of the Cajal-Retzius cells. The bottom half becomes the subplate.
scenes.visual: Upper half labelled marginal zone (future layer 1, Cajal-Retzius cells). Lower half labelled subplate.
scenes.narration: The top half becomes the marginal zone, future layer 1, home of the Cajal-Retzius cells. The bottom half becomes the subplate.

scenes.tts: Between them, the cortical plate becomes layers two to six. Each new neuron climbs up from below to reach it.
scenes.caption: Between them, the cortical plate becomes layers 2 to 6. Each new neuron climbs up from below to reach it.
scenes.visual: The band between marginal zone and subplate labelled cortical plate, layers 2 to 6. A neuron climbs a radial fibre from the ventricular zone into it.
scenes.narration: Between them, the cortical plate becomes layers 2 to 6. Each new neuron climbs up from below to reach it.

scenes.tts: Layers are numbered from the surface down, layer one on top. In the cortical plate, they are made the other way, from six up to two.
scenes.caption: Layers are numbered from the surface down, layer 1 on top. In the cortical plate, they are made the other way, from 6 up to 2.
scenes.visual: Layer numbers 1 to 6 drop in from the top down along the side of the column; a curved arrow points from 6 up toward 2. Label: cortical plate made 6 first, 2 last; layer 1 from the early preplate.
scenes.narration: Layers are numbered from the surface down, layer 1 on top. In the cortical plate, they are made the other way, from 6 up to 2.

scenes.tts: The map raises three puzzles. First, who came first? How can you tell?
scenes.visual: Return to the cortical wall. Puzzle card 1: Who came first?
scenes.narration: The map raises three puzzles. First, who came first? How can you tell?

scenes.tts: Second, record or cause? Does the progenitor carry its own schedule, or do its surroundings decide?
scenes.visual: Puzzle card 2: Record or cause? A progenitor with a small calendar inside it, beside surrounding cells sending arrows inward.
scenes.narration: Second, record or cause? Does the progenitor carry its own schedule, or do its surroundings decide?

scenes.tts: Third, how many of each? How does one pool make a few neurons, then many, as it first grows and then shrinks?
scenes.visual: Puzzle card 3: How many of each? A pool of progenitors that swells, then shrinks, with a trickle and then a stream of neurons coming out.
scenes.narration: Third, how many of each? How does one pool make a few neurons, then many, as it first grows and then shrinks?

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea to carry. A birthday marks a time. The progenitor's state at that time sets the neuron's temporal identity.
scenes.visual: Guiding-idea card: A birthday marks a time; the progenitor's state at that time sets the neuron's temporal identity, its layer included.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea to carry. A birthday marks a time. The progenitor's state at that time sets the neuron's temporal identity.

scenes.tts: The birthday instructs nothing. It is a timestamp. In ferret grafts, laminar fate becomes fixed late in the final cell cycle. Migration and later programs then build the layer.
scenes.visual: A clock stamp on a neuron labelled timestamp. A cell-cycle ring beside it, the last turn shaded: ferret grafts, laminar responsiveness becomes restricted late in the final cycle.
scenes.narration: The birthday instructs nothing. It is a timestamp. In ferret grafts, laminar fate becomes fixed late in the final cell cycle. Migration and later programs then build the layer.

scenes.tts: That state has two parts: what the progenitor can still make, its competence, and the cues it reads.
scenes.visual: The progenitor shown with a short menu card labelled competence, and arrows from neighbouring cells labelled cues.
scenes.narration: That state has two parts: what the progenitor can still make, its competence, and the cues it reads.

scenes.tts: In the cortical plate, the earlier the birthday, the deeper the layer. The neuron keeps maturing after it is born.
scenes.visual: Early neuron settles in layer 6, a later one in layer 2. Label: earlier birthday, deeper layer (cortical plate). Small note: maturing continues after birth.
scenes.narration: In the cortical plate, the earlier the birthday, the deeper the layer. The neuron keeps maturing after it is born.

scenes.tts: And in normal development, the progenitor's menu gets shorter with time.
scenes.visual: The menu card loses its top lines one by one. Label: in normal development.
scenes.narration: And in normal development, the progenitor's menu gets shorter with time.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: cortical-plate neurons are born near the ventricle and climb. Layers six to two are made in that order.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card over the full wall: excitatory neurons start in the zones beside the ventricle; cortical-plate layers made 6 first, 2 last.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: cortical-plate neurons are born near the ventricle and climb. Layers 6 to 2 are made in that order.
scenes.caption: The takeaway: cortical-plate neurons are born near the ventricle and climb. Layers 6 to 2 are made in that order.
